Upon which suppositions some of our later historians have had the weakness to compute, that it had its origin 1107 years before the birth of Christ; 600 years before the fall of the Assyrian empire by the death of Belshazzar, and 350 before the building of Rome.

arxiv-1401-3941.title: Network Coding for 3 3 s / n /n t Sum-Networks
arxiv-1401-3941.creator: Wentu Song 1 , Chau Yuen 1 , Kai Cai 2 , and Rongquan Feng 3
arxiv-1401-3941.description: Abstract A sum-network is a directed acyclic network where each source independently generates one symbol from a given field 𝔽 \mathbb{F} and each terminal wants to receive the sum ( ( over OPEN 𝔽 ) \mathbb{F}) of the source symbols.

arxiv-1809-07705.title: On convergence and rational summation of power series in p-adic field
arxiv-1809-07705.creator: Absos Ali Shaikh 1, MABUD ALI SARKAR 2
arxiv-1809-07705.description: Abstract . In this paper we have discussed convergence of power series both in p-adic norm as well as real norm. We have investigated rational summability of power series with respect to both p-adic norm and real norm under certain conditions. Then we have studied convergence of specially constructed power series and derived summation formula.

arxiv-2101-07086.title: Model Compression for Domain Adaptation through Causal Effect Estimation
arxiv-2101-07086.creator: Guy Rotman, Amir Feder, Roi Reichart
arxiv-2101-07086.description: Abstract Recent improvements in the predictive quality of natural language processing systems are often dependent on a substantial increase in the number of model parameters. This has led to various attempts of compressing such models, but existing methods have not considered the differences in the predictive power of various model components or in the generalizability of the compressed models.

arxiv-2107-12064.title: How Knowledge Graph and Attention Help? A Quantitative Analysis into Bag-level Relation Extraction
arxiv-2107-12064.creator: Zikun Hu, Yixin Cao, Lifu Huang, Tat-Seng Chua
arxiv-2107-12064.description: Abstract Knowledge Graph (KG) and attention mechanism have been demonstrated effective in introducing and selecting useful information for weakly supervised methods. However, only qualitative analysis and ablation study are provided as evidence. In this paper, we contribute a dataset and propose a paradigm to quantitatively evaluate the effect of attention and KG on bag-level relation extraction (RE).

arxiv-2111-10283.title: The Joy of Neural Painting
arxiv-2111-10283.creator: Ernesto Diaz-Aviles, Claudia Orellana-Rodriguez, Beth Jochim
arxiv-2111-10283.description: Abstract Neural Painters is a class of models that follows a GAN framework to generate brushstrokes, which are then composed to create paintings. GANs are great generative models for AI Art but they are known to be notoriously difficult to train.

arxiv-2204-09738.title: Res-CNN-BiLSTM Network for overcoming Mental Health Disturbances caused due to Cyberbullying through Social Media
arxiv-2204-09738.creator: Raunak Joshi, Abhishek Gupta, Nandan Kanvinde
arxiv-2204-09738.description: Abstract Mental Health Disturbance has many reasons and cyberbullying is one of the major causes that does exploitation using social media as an instrument. The cyberbullying is done on the basis of Religion, Ethnicity, Age and Gender which is a sensitive psychological issue.

arxiv-2207-09786.title: Non-Uniform Diffusion Models
arxiv-2207-09786.creator: Georgios Batzolis, Jan Stanczuk, Carola-Bibiane Schönlieb, Christian Etmann
arxiv-2207-09786.description: Abstract Diffusion models have emerged as one of the most promising frameworks for deep generative modeling. In this work, we explore the potential of non-uniform diffusion models. We show that non-uniform diffusion leads to multi-scale diffusion models which have similar structure to this of multi-scale normalizing flows.

arxiv-2209-12784.title: Outage Analysis on Type I HARQ over Time-Correlated Rayleigh Fading Channels
arxiv-2209-12784.creator: Zheng Shi, Shaodan Ma, Kam-Weng Tam
arxiv-2209-12784.description: Abstract This paper analyzes Type I hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) over time-correlated Rayleigh fading channels. Due to the presence of channel time correlation, the analysis is more challenging than the prior analysis in the literature. Outage probability is first derived as a weighted sum of joint CDF of multiple independent Gamma random variables based on an infinite series representation.

arxiv-2209-13721.title: Stochastic model for barrier crossings and fluctuations in local timescale.
arxiv-2209-13721.creator: Rajeev Bhaskaran, Vijay Ganesh Sadhasivam
arxiv-2209-13721.description: Abstract The problem of computing the rate of diffusion-aided activated barrier crossings between metastable states is one of broad relevance in physical sciences. The transition path formalism aims to compute the rate of these events by analysing the statistical properties of the transition path between the two metastable regions concerned.

arxiv-2405-18036.title: ForecastGrapher: Redefining Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2405-18036.creator: Wanlin Cai, Kun Wang, Hao Wu, Xiaoxu Chen, Yuankai Wu
arxiv-2405-18036.description: Abstract The challenge of effectively learning inter-series correlations for multivariate time series forecasting remains a substantial and unresolved problem. Traditional deep learning models, which are largely dependent on the Transformer paradigm for modeling long sequences, often fail to integrate information from multiple time series into a coherent and universally applicable model.

arxiv-2407-01937.title: Efficient-Empathy: Towards Efficient and Effective Selection of Empathy Data
arxiv-2407-01937.creator: Linzhuang Sun †§ , Hao Liang †‡ , Jingxuan Wei § , Linkun Sun ⋄ , Bihui Yu § , Bin Cui ‡∗ , Wentao Zhang ‡∗
arxiv-2407-01937.description: Abstract . In recent years, with the rapid advancements in large language models (LLMs), achieving excellent empathetic response capability has become a crucial prerequisite. Consequently, managing and understanding empathetic datasets has gained increasing importance. However, empathetic data are typically trained without any quality selection, leading to inefficient data usage and wasted computational resources.

arxiv-2408-00252.title: Quantum thermalization and Floquet engineering in a spin ensemble with a clock transition
arxiv-2408-00252.creator: Mi Lei, Rikuto Fukumori, Chun-Ju Wu, Edwin Barnes, Sophia Economou, Joonhee Choi, Andrei Faraon
arxiv-2408-00252.description: Abstract Studying and controlling quantum many-body interactions is fundamentally important for quantum science and related emerging technologies. Optically addressable solid-state spins offer a promising platform for exploring various quantum many-body phenomena due to their scalability to a large Hilbert space.

Bagley, Eduardo Bañados, Rachana Bhatawdekar, Madisyn Brooks, Antonello Calabrò, Óscar A. Chávez Ortiz, Yingjie Cheng, Nikko J. Cleri, Justin
arxiv-2409-06772.description: Abstract We present a sample of 62 H α \alpha detected broad-line active galactic nuclei (BLAGN) at redshifts 3.5 < z < 6.8 3.5<z<6.8 using data from the CEERS and RUBIES surveys. We select these sources directly from JWST /NIRSpec G395M/F290LP spectra.

arxiv-2504-05496.title: A Survey on Hypothesis Generation for Scientific Discovery in the Era of Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-05496.creator: Atilla Kaan Alkan, Shashwat Sourav, Maja Jablonska, Simone Astarita, Rishabh Chakrabarty, Nikhil Garuda, Pranav Khetarpal, Maciej Pióro, Dimitrios Tanoglidis, Kartheik G. Iyer, Mugdha S. Polimera, Michael J. Smith, Tirthankar Ghosal, Marc Huertas-Company, Sandor Kruk, Kevin Schawinski & Ioana Ciucă
arxiv-2504-05496.description: Abstract Hypothesis generation is a fundamental step in scientific discovery, yet it is increasingly challenged by information overload and disciplinary fragmentation. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have sparked growing interest in their potential to enhance and automate this process.

arxiv-2504-14542.title: A Lightweight Neural Network for Accelerating Radiative Transfer Modeling in WRF * Thanks:
arxiv-2504-14542.creator: Erick Fredj 1 2 , Iggy Segev Gal 2 , Noam Lavi 2 , Shahar Belkar 2 , Mark Wasserman 2 , Ding Zhaohui 2 , Yann Delorme 2
arxiv-2504-14542.description: Abstract Radiative transfer calculations in weather and climate models are notoriously complex and computationally intensive, which poses significant challenges. Traditional methods, while accurate, can be prohibitively slow, necessitating the development of more efficient alternatives. Recently, empirical emulators based on neural networks (NN) have been proposed as a solution to this problem.

arxiv-2508-06527.title: Half-life Measurements of Highly Charged Radioisotopes by Nuclear Recoil in a Penning Trap
arxiv-2508-06527.creator: Scott Moroch, Carolyn Chun, Doug VanDerwerken, Ariana Shearin, Brian L. Beaudoin, Klaus Blaum, Timothy W. Koeth
arxiv-2508-06527.description: Abstract We present a novel method for measuring the half-life of highly charged radioisotopes by non-destructive nuclear recoil detection in a Penning ion trap. A specific emphasis is placed on Be 3 + 7 \rm{}^{7}Be^{3+} , which plays a crucial role in stellar evolution and the production of solar neutrinos.

arxiv-2509-26146.title: Ordinal Label-Distribution Learning with Constrained Asymmetric Priors for Imbalanced Retinal Grading
arxiv-2509-26146.creator: Nagur Shareef Shaik, Teja Krishna Cherukuri, Adnan Masood, Ehsan Adeli, Dong Hye Ye
arxiv-2509-26146.description: Abstract Diabetic retinopathy grading is inherently ordinal and long-tailed, with minority stages being scarce, heterogeneous, and clinically critical to detect accurately. Conventional methods often rely on isotropic Gaussian priors and symmetric loss functions, misaligning latent representations with the task’s asymmetric nature.

europmc-pmc535701.creator: Taheri S, Lin L, Austin D, Young T, Mignot E.
europmc-pmc535701.description: Background Sleep duration may be an important regulator of body weight and metabolism. An association between short habitual sleep time and increased body mass index (BMI) has been reported in large population samples. The potential role of metabolic hormones in this...

europmc-pmc5472696.creator: Huang S, Chaudhary K, Garmire LX.
europmc-pmc5472696.description: Multi-omics data integration is one of the major challenges in the era of precision medicine. Considerable work has been done with the advent of high-throughput studies, which have enabled the data access for downstream analyses. To improve the clinical outcome prediction, a...

pmc-11551454.title: Carfilzomib-induced pulmonary hypertension in a patient with multiple myeloma
pmc-11551454.creator: Kosuke Uruno, Hiroyuki Iwano, Toshiaki Hayashi, Ryosuke Hatano, Kaoru Komuro, Kandoh Kawahatsu, Takahiro Doi, Satoshi Yuda
pmc-11551454.description: A 59-year-old female being treated for multiple myeloma (MM) was referred to the Division of Cardiology due to edema and dyspnea. She developed dyspnea on exertion 2 months previously when carfilzomib, a second-generation selective proteasome inhibitor which was approved for treatment of relapsed and refractory MM, was introduced, and facial edema appeared thereafter.

pmc-12541940.title: Serial mediation of perceived stress and depression in the relationship between childhood trauma and mobile phone addiction among undergraduate nursing students in China: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey
pmc-12541940.creator: Hongna Li, Xiuhuan Wang, Wenjin Chen, Na Li, Jinghui Tong, Jiao Fang, Haitao Wen, Jue Wang, Chunni Heng, Xiujuan Feng, Meifang Wang, Qing Zhao, Wenkai Zheng
pmc-12541940.description: BackgroundNurses are critical front-line members of the healthcare workforce in China. Investigating mobile phone addiction (MPA) among nursing undergraduates is essential, as it may hinder their professional development and exacerbate the current nursing shortage. Understanding this issue is crucial for safeguarding future healthcare workforce sustainability. Therefore, it is necessary to examine the contributing factors of MPA and clarify their interrelationships.

pmc-12995794.title: Efficacy and safety of through-the-scope twin clip for endoscopic closure of gastrointestinal defects
pmc-12995794.creator: Chenyang Li, Yan Xu, Zhongrui Xu, Yujie Feng, Tao Wang, Fuxiu Huang, Ningning Zhang, Chuangxin Zhang, Sang Zhou, Shuling Li, Chao Chen
pmc-12995794.description: Background and aimsThe widespread adoption of endoscopic therapy has made the closure of gastrointestinal defects a critical limiting factor for its advancement. Recently, a novel device—the through-the-scope twin clip (TTS-TC)—has been introduced for endoscopic defect closure. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of TTS-TC.

pmc-13341190.title: BRAF Mutation and Tumor Growth Kinetics during Active Surveillance of Papillary Thyroid Microcarcinoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
pmc-13341190.creator: Jinyoung Kim, Min Kyoung Lee, Tae-Jung Kim, Dong-Jun Lim, Ki-Hyun Baek
pmc-13341190.description: BackgroundWe investigated tumor volume doubling time (TVDT) during active surveillance of papillary thyroid microcarcinoma (PTMC) and reviewed clinical factors including BRAF mutation associated with tumor progression.MethodsPatients with PTMC who deferred surgery for more than 1 year after diagnosis between 2014 and 2021 and were followed until 2023 were enrolled.

pmc-13363767.title: A Hybrid Edge–Cloud Intelligence Framework for Reliable AI-Driven Sensing and Data Fusion in Smart Healthcare and Urban Environments
pmc-13363767.creator: Fahd M. Aldosari
pmc-13363767.description: Healthcare and urban infrastructure are increasingly supported by Internet of Things-based sensing systems, in which heterogeneous physiological, environmental, and transmission-level data require reliable, low-latency processing. Existing works typically treat medical IoT sensing, smart-city anomaly detection, or edge-cloud offloading as isolated problems, thereby failing to support integrated sensing scenarios in shared smart environments.

pmc-13377713.title: Extensive-stage small cell esophageal carcinoma: a retrospective analysis of treatment modalities
pmc-13377713.creator: Di Liu, Xiaofei Zhang, Junhua Zhang, Kuaile Zhao, Jiaqing Xiang, Zhen Zhang, Yiliang Zhang
pmc-13377713.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to investigate the clinicopathological features, treatment strategies and outcomes, failure patterns, and prognostic factors impacting progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with extensive-stage primary small cell esophageal carcinoma (ES-SCEC).MethodsThis retrospective study included consecutive patients with ES-SCEC diagnosed and treated at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center from January 2006 to December 2024.
